### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 182)

Jedd Fisch and the Huskies improved from 6-7 to 9-4 in his second season and the Huskies looked primed and ready perhaps to challenge the top of the Big Ten with 65% of its production back. Then, days after signing a $4 million NIL deal to return to Washington, quarterback Demond Williams Jr. announced he was entering the transfer portal and was reportedly about to sign for more money with LSU. Fortunately for all parties, this did not end up in court and Williams returned to Seattle. Three of the four losses last season came against top-25 teams. Washington has gotten itself to the upper level of the Big Ten in just its third year in the conference, but it is now time for them to take the next step and knock off some of the league’s elite. Having Williams back is certainly a necessary step for that to happen. Over 7.5 Washington opens with a full September slate at home so they should start 4-0 before the trip to USC. Perhaps that gets its confidence rolling into the season and the Huskies can finally knock off a good team. The Huskies only averaged 9.3 points per game and 4.3 yards per play against Ohio State, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Oregon, who were the four best defenses they faced. Simply put, Williams also must be better against the better teams.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 183)*, with the answers as written:

### Is Demond Williams Jr. all-in?

NIL and transfer portal are the way of the world in college football today. However, this got perilously close to Williams leaving and lawyers were about to get involved. Williams got some bad advice from his representatives and perhaps all of that is behind him. Can everyone let bygones be bygones? If so, Williams is one of the more dynamic quarterbacks in the conference. He led the Huskies last season to top-five marks in both scoring offense (No. 4, 34.1 PPG) and total offense (No. 5, 409.9 YPG), but this time around he must do it without his best players from last season including wide receiver Denzel Boston and running back Jonah Coleman. Receiver Dezmen Roebuck (42-560-7) and tight end Decker DeGraaf (32-360- 2) are back and four-star receivers Jordan Clay, Mason James, and Trez Davis are part of Washington’s highest-rated recruiting class in school history.

### Who emerges at running back?

Jonah Coleman is off to the NFL and his heir apparent Adam Mohammed transferred to Cal. They added seniors Jayden Limar (Oregon) and Trey Cooley (Troy) out of the portal, but both missed the spring with injuries and Jordan Washington (27-233-1) was also injured in spring ball, so redshirt freshman Quaid Carr and true freshman Brian Bonner got most of the reps. Whoever emerges in the backfield should have a very good offensive line to run behind as four starters return including the Hatchett brothers – center Landen and right guard Geirean – plus five-star freshman Kodi Greene should start at left tackle.

### Can the Huskies beat anyone good?

Washington has shown the ability to beat the teams that they are supposed to beat, but this is a program still looking for a signature victory to get the Husky faithful to fully believe in Fisch. The Huskies are just 2-7 in Big Ten road games under Fisch with the two victories coming last year at Maryland and at UCLA. This year there are tests at USC, at Oregon, and at Nebraska and hosting Indiana in the home finale. Much will depend on Williams, who had just 645 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions in Washington’s four defeats.
